trial_court: Court of JMFC-02, North West District, Rohini Courts, Delhi - Case No. 3473/17

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: S/o Sh. Ashok Kumar, R/o H. No.500, Ground Floor, Orchid Island, Artemis Hospital, Sector 51, Islampur, Gurgaon, Haryana.
parties.respondent_defendant: S/o Late Sh. N. L. Thakur, R/o T-6, Top Floor, Shimla Hotel, Himachal Pradesh.

facts_of_case: Complainant provided loan to accused and issued cheque which was dishonoured. Accused failed to pay despite legal demand notice.

legal_principles.principle: It is wrong to suggest that a person is deposing falsely due to contradictions in the source of his funds.
legal_principles.held: He was financially capable of granting the loan. It was correct to say that he had ₹90,000 in his bank account on 24.10.2013. It was also correct that he had received ₹4,00,000 in his account from Ashok Kumar Tyagi on 25.10.2013.

legal_principles.principle: A person's statement that he did not maintain any diary regarding the loan amount is credible.
legal_principles.held: Voluntarily, he stated that it was a friendly loan. He did not maintain any diary regarding the loan amount.

legal_principles.principle: A person's statement that he did not know the details of a cheque being filled in by someone else is credible.
legal_principles.held: Voluntarily, he stated that he did not know whether the details were filled in by the accused or someone else.

outcome.final_order: Accused convicted for offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

use_for_drafting: drafting a complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
defending an accused in a cheque bounce case
advising on legal remedies for a bounced cheque
